To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) bursts in primary sensory neurons are behaviorally relevant, 2) bursts in primary neurons perform better as a feature detector than isolated spikes, 3) bursts in primary afferents are correlated, and 4) the correlated bursts in the primary afferents may result in a correlated burst in the interneuron.

bursts in the primary sensory neurons of the auditory system of the cricket Teleogyllus oceanicus signal salient stimulus features and that these bursts are correlated between neurons, suggesting that they might serve as a mechanism of feature binding.

(i) primary auditory interneurons in the crickets' auditory neuropile produce bursts in response to ultrasound stimuli, (ii) these bursts are more effective in signaling conspicuous increases in stimulus amplitude than isolated spikes, (iii) the temporal correlation between bursts in primary auditory neurons and in AN2 is high, and (iv) bursts are temporally correlated between primary auditory neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the temporal structure of sensory spike trains is shaped by the stimulus, and how this structure is used by the brain for the computation of stimulus features.
the coding of behaviorally relevant stimulus features by the temporal structure of spike trains in interneurons.
the question of how the nervous system can detect salient stimulus features, and we have found that this is done by the temporal structure of spike trains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bursting in sensory neurons is behaviorally relevant, as it is in interneurons, and that it is an important component of the neuronal processing of salient stimulus features in the cricket auditory system.
bursts in AN2 and sensory neurons are not just a consequence of the intrinsic dynamics of the neuron, but are behaviorally relevant and can be used to code for stimulus features.
bursts are a general coding strategy of primary sensory neurons and interneurons of the auditory system of T. oceanicus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal structure of spike trains is not only a property of interneurons, but also of sensory neurons.
the temporal structure of spike trains in the cricket auditory system is shaped at the earliest level of sensory processing.
bursts in primary auditory sensory neurons code for salient stimulus features, which are subsequently used to trigger behavioral responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the temporal structure of spike trains can be used for information coding at the earliest level of processing, and that the information is not lost during processing, but is preserved in the spike trains of higher order neurons.
bursting is a feature of sensory neurons and that this feature is behaviorally relevant.
the neural code for salient stimulus features is not limited to higher-order processing stages but is already present in the sensory periphery.
